defects.claim: Recovering from a failed setter in a multi-parameter update re-applies the setters that already succeeded, so each runs twice
A partially failed graph start leaves the healthy sources playing while the runner's state stays paused
defects.scenario: a pipeline with two sources, one of whose `start` throws (an `AudioGraph.start` contract case: "A source whose start throws is left stopped while the rest start, and the first error is rethrown"). `play()` calls `graph.start()`, which throws after starting the other sources, so `set({ playing: true })` never runs and the promise rejects. The graph is audibly playing, but `state.playing` is false: `useFollowAudioRunner` never starts its preview loop, a UI shows a Play button for sound already playing, and the failing stage gets no error in the run. It should publish `playing: true` (the graph is running) and report the failed stage under `errors`, as `applyStructure` does for a source that fails to start.
defects.cause: exception from a partial start skips the state update

defects.claim: nextStageId mints an id a cluster already has, so adding a stage makes that cluster vanish
defects.scenario: a doc has a cluster whose id is `blur` (or `audio.gain`, any id equal to a stage type name; clusters from a loaded file can be named anything). `EffectEditorApi.addStage(blurType)` calls `nextStageId(d.pipeline, 'blur')`, which checks only `p.stages`, so the new stage gets id `blur`. Now a stage and a cluster share an id: `checkPipeline` reports `duplicate-cluster` ("has the id of a stage"), `uniqueClusters` drops the cluster from every look, and `editorScene.clusterOf` answers `undefined` for it, so the user's group disappears and can no longer be edited. It should have minted `blur-2`, as `nextClusterId` already does in the other direction by excluding stage ids.
defects.cause: id-taken set omits cluster ids

defects.claim: moveRunInChain picks a moved run's unwired main port without regard to type or control, refusing valid moves
defects.scenario: the stage being moved is the head of the main chain (`i === 0`, so `mainIn` has no entry for it), and its first open input is a control-typed port, for example inputs `[{ id: 'amount', type: 'number' }, { id: 'in', type: 'image' }]` with `number` marked `control`. Dragging it into the middle of the chain gives `sIn = pick(first, 'inputs')`, which is `'amount'`. The wire into it, a→first, reuses `wAB`'s data output (`aOut = p.wires[wAB].from.port`, an image port). `canWire` then sees `image` ≠ `number` and the move returns `null`, so the drop is refused even though `'in'` would take the wire. The same happens on the `sOut = pick(last, 'outputs')` side for a run whose last stage is the chain's tail and whose first output is control-typed. The code should pick a non-control port, or one matching the type of the neighbor it is being wired to (the `type` argument `pick` already accepts).
defects.cause: port pick ignores the neighbor's type and control wires

defects.claim: clusterContents and clusterParents disagree with how clusters are drawn when a member is named twice or clusters loop
defects.scenario: stage `s` is listed in cluster A and again in cluster B (A first). `nestClusters` (packages/diagram/src/clusterTree.ts:48) draws `s` only in A. `clusterContents(doc, 'B')` still counts `s`, so dragging B's box under nodeGraph (`dragEdit` → `moveCluster`) also moves `s`, which is drawn inside A. `clusterRuns`/`clusterGripOf` read the same over-broad membership. For a loop (A holds B, B holds A), `nestClusters` drops B's claim on A, so A is drawn at the top level. `clusterParents` still records B as A's parent, so `clusterDepth` and `clusterSlotsAt`'s sibling set are computed against a tree the drawing does not have. Both inputs are ones `checkPipeline` reports but a doc can still hold, and the editor draws them. The rule for who holds what is decided once in `nestClusters`, and again, differently, here.
defects.cause: second definition of cluster membership diverges from nestClusters

defects.claim: canConnect counts an id-less or repeated-id wire as feeding its own input while its end is dragged
defects.scenario: doc has an id-less wire `src.out → gain.in` (or a second wire repeating an earlier wire's id), `gain.in` takes one wire. The user drags that wire's `from` end to another output. `except` is `built.wireOf(moving.edge)`, the id the wire gets in `ensureWireIds(doc)` (e.g. `w1`), but `fed` filters `now().doc.pipeline.wires` — the raw doc, where the wire's id is `undefined` (or the earlier wire's id). The filter keeps the moving wire, `inputFed` sees `gain.in` already fed, and `canConnect` refuses every target, so the reconnect can never be made. `onReconnect` itself runs on `ensureWireIds(d)` and would accept it; the two disagree on which wire is being moved. Should test against `ensureWireIds(doc).pipeline`.
defects.cause: raw doc ids compared with ensured ids

defects.claim: Live audio previews always land on port `out` regardless of the stage's actual output port name
defects.scenario: a caller passes its own `nodes` (`LiveAudioRunnerOptions.nodes`, `AudioStageNodes` keyed by any stage type) for a stage whose output port is `signal`, not `out`. While playing with previews on, every frame draws a bitmap into `stages[id].previews.out`. The look keeps its preview slot under `previewRowId('signal')`, so nothing ever shows in that slot. A new bitmap is still made every frame for a key nobody reads. The preview should go to the stage's shown port (its first output, as `shownPorts` gives).
defects.cause: port id hard-coded; previews never see the pipeline

defects.claim: A bypassed stage whose ports are not typed `audio` cuts the signal instead of passing it through
defects.scenario: with custom `nodes`, a stage type whose ports are typed something else (e.g. `signal`) sits mid-chain and has `bypassed: true`. `firstAudio` is `undefined`, so `fed` keeps only wires where `w.to.port === undefined`, which is none. The stage has inputs and nothing fed, so the plan `continue`s without setting `origins`. Everything downstream then has no origin and is left out, so bypassing the stage silences the chain. It should carry its first input through. `played` itself never checks port types, so these stages otherwise play normally.
defects.cause: bypass pass-through keyed to the literal port type 'audio'

defects.claim: A wire id equal to a stage id (or a minted id colliding across the wire and stage namespaces) makes diagramScene throw, and checkPipeline never reports the collision
defects.scenario: a doc with a stage whose id is `w1` (any user-chosen id) and no wires; the user connects two ports in `EffectEditor`. `addWire` → `nextWireId` checks only wire ids and mints `w1`. `wireEdges`/`drawableWires` keep the wire's id as the edge id, so the edge spec and the stage's node spec are both `w1`, and `diagramScene` throws "two things would share the scene id \"w1\"" (fromData.ts:249): the editor and `EffectChart` crash on the next render. The same happens for a loaded pipeline whose wire id equals a stage or cluster id, and `ensureWireIds` mints the same way. Likewise `nextStageId` avoids only stage ids: adding a stage whose type id equals an existing cluster id (a hand-written cluster `source`, then Add stage "source") makes `uniqueClusters` silently drop that cluster and its box. Expected: minted ids avoid every id sharing the scene's id space (stages, clusters, wires), and `checkPipeline` reports a wire id that names a stage or cluster, as it does a cluster id naming a stage.
defects.cause: id minting checks only its own namespace

defects.claim: Reordering lanes drops every laneOrder entry whose type has no stage yet
defects.scenario: doc.laneOrder is `['mask', 'image', 'number']` and the pipeline currently has no mask stage. `lanes` draws only used types (`laneTypes` keeps the `first` the pipeline uses), so the drawn lane order is image, number. Dragging number above image calls `setLaneOrder(doc, ['number', 'image'])`, erasing `mask`; adding a mask stage later puts its lane last instead of first. Expected: the move reorders the drawn lanes and keeps the undrawn entries of `doc.laneOrder` (and the options' `lanes`) where they were.
defects.cause: lane order rebuilt from drawn lanes only

defects.claim: An edit that changes the errors while paused wipes the previews already drawn, and they stay blank until play
defects.scenario: previews on 'scope', play, pause: the last frame's scopes stay on the stages. Now edit a stage so it errors (or clear an error): `publishErrors` publishes `errorsRun(next)`, a run with no previews, so every scope on the chart disappears; `frame` only runs while playing, so nothing redraws them until the user plays again. Expected: an error change keeps the previews of the run it replaces (or redraws from the taps), so the frozen scopes stay up.
defects.cause: errors-only run replaces preview run

defects.claim: checkPipeline does not report a cluster that names the same member twice
defects.scenario: `clusters: [{ id: 'g', members: ['a', 'a'] }]`: the second `a` finds `holder.get('a') === 'g'` and the `first !== cluster.id` test skips it, so no problem is reported, though `duplicate-member` exists for a member held twice and the repeat reaches the looks and `dissolveCluster` (which then splices `a` into the parent twice). Expected: a `duplicate-member` problem for the repeat.
defects.cause: same-cluster repeat exempted

defects.claim: Live audio runner draws every scope and spectrum at the default 48-unit size, ignoring the look's previewSize
defects.scenario: a chart or editor whose look sets `showPreviews: true, previewSize: { width: 160, height: 48 }` (or `96`) shows a live audio pipeline from `useLiveAudioRunner`. The slot is laid out at 160×48, but `draw` paints each tap at `PREVIEW_SIZE` × `PREVIEW_SIZE` (48×48 → 96×96 device px), so the bitmap is stretched: a wide slot gets a distorted waveform, and a larger square slot gets a blurry one. The image runner takes the same setting as an option (`runner/pass.ts:23`, `useEffectRunner`'s `previewSize`). `LiveAudioRunnerOptions`/`UseLiveAudioRunnerOptions` have no matching field, so the option is dropped on this path.
defects.cause: preview size hard-coded; no option threaded through

defects.claim: A structural batch the graph refuses blocks every param write in that sync and every later sync until the structure changes
defects.scenario: the graph refuses a structural patch during `graph.check`, for example a custom `AudioStageNode.build` that hands back a def already in use (`defInUse`). `landed` is then false, so `sets` is `[]` and `plan` stays `from`. Every later `setPipeline` re-diffs from that same `from`, rebuilds the same refused structure, and is refused again. While that persists, no level change to any other stage reaches the graph. If `failingStage` finds no quoted id in the message, no stage gets an error either, and the only sign is a `console.warn`. Sets on nodes that are unchanged in both plans could still be applied.
defects.cause: param writes gated on the whole structural batch landing

defects.claim: clusterStages deletes a boxed cluster it empties, whereas moveToCluster keeps it
defects.scenario: under `nodeGraph`, cluster `P` has a `clusterBoxes` entry and holds only stage `A`; stage `B` is top level. `EffectEditorApi.cluster(['A', 'B'])` → the members have different parents, so `pruneClusters(clusters, taken)` runs with no `keep`, `P` is emptied and dropped, and `withClusters` drops its box too. Dragging `A` out of `P` instead goes through `moveToCluster`, whose `boxed` keep leaves `P` and its box in place. The same question, whether a boxed cluster survives being emptied, gets two answers. Taking members out for a new group should keep a boxed `P`, as a drag does.
defects.cause: pruneClusters called without the boxed keep

defects.claim: Renaming a cluster whose label has leading or trailing spaces records a 'Rename group' edit when nothing changed
defects.scenario: a doc loaded with cluster label `" Mix "` (docShape accepts any string). The user opens the rename field and presses Enter, or clicks away, without typing. `ClusterTitleField` hands back `text.trim()` = `"Mix"`, and `"Mix" !== " Mix "`, so `onChange` gets a doc and an undo entry for an edit the user never made. It should compare against the trimmed label, or not trim.
defects.cause: trimmed text compared to untrimmed label

defects.claim: Clearing a route that does not exist still sends an 'Edit route' edit under nodeGraph
defects.scenario: under `nodeGraph`, a wire with no entry in `doc.routes` reports a `RouteChange` with empty `waypoints`. `setWireRoute(d, id, [])` returns a new doc with `routes: {}`, and `commit` hands it to `onChange` as 'Edit route': an undo entry that changes nothing, and an empty `routes` written into the doc. The rack/lanes branch just above returns `null` for the same case (`was === undefined`), so each look answers it differently.
defects.cause: no no-op check on the nodeGraph path

defects.claim: The cluster reorder counts order items that have no drawn box as drawn, while the stage reorder drops them
defects.scenario: the stage reorder passes `drawnOrder(order, boxOf)` to `stageMove`, so only items with a drawn box count as "drawn" (the comment at `drawnOrder` says a move's indices count only these). `clusterReorder` passes the raw `order` to `clusterMove`, and `drawnOf(order)` there treats an item with no box as drawn. `dropInGap` then stops trying gaps at that stage, and `indices(before, true)` counts it. A look item without a box (one not yet laid out, or one the look leaves undrawn) can therefore make a cluster drop that the stage path would accept come back `null`, or land in a different gap. The two reorders read "drawn" differently.
defects.cause: drawnOrder filter not applied on the cluster path

defects.claim: checkPipeline does not report two wires feeding an input that does not accept many
defects.scenario: a pipeline loaded from a file has wires a.out→b.in and c.out→b.in, where `b.in` has no `many`. The editor treats that input as already fed (`inputFed`/`canWire` in edit.ts refuse a second wire), and the runner reads only one value for a non-`many` input, but `checkPipeline` reports nothing, `drawableWires` draws neither wire as a problem, and `onProblems` says the pipeline is fine. The same question ("may this input take a second wire?") gets two different answers. checkPipeline should report the second wire (for example as a new `kind`) so the drawing flags it.
defects.cause: fan-in rule enforced only in the editor

defects.claim: typeColors uses up a series color for every type that already has its own color, so later types get shifted colors
defects.scenario: the colors are `{ image: '#fff' }` and the ports, in order, are `image` then `number`. `colors.size` counts `image`, so `number` gets `series[1]` and `series[0]` is never used. With one given type per pipeline, the documented "next in `series`" order is shifted by one for every given color before it.
defects.cause: series index counts given colors

defects.claim: A delay node's maximum delay time is fixed when it is built, so a time later raised as a level past that maximum is not honored
defects.scenario: `time` is a level, so editing it sends a `set` patch and never a rebuild. `createDelayNode` fixes `maxTime = max(2000, time)` when it is built. Built at 300 ms and then set to 5000 ms, the live graph clamps the delay at 2000 ms. After `reset`, or any rebuild of that node, the same pipeline plays a 5000 ms delay. One pipeline plays two ways depending on how it got there.
defects.cause: build-time max for a live level
